summary: This bill requires federal courts to impose lifetime no-contact orders on any defendant convicted of a felony crime of violence or specified sexual offense, barring all direct or indirect communication or interaction with the victim for the rest of the defendant's life, terminable only upon pardon, commutation, or overturned conviction.

The bill directly amends federal criminal procedure by mandating lifetime no-contact injunctions for victims of covered violent and sexual felonies. This imposes stricter, permanent post-conviction restrictions on offenders and treats violations as contempt of court. It aligns with tougher sentencing and victim-protection measures rather than rehabilitation-focused reforms.
The bill has no provisions concerning trade, tariffs, or globalization.

While the definition of 'contact' includes electronic and digital means, the bill is narrowly focused on criminal no-contact orders and does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or surveillance policy.
No content relates to workers' rights, unions, or employment regulations.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or discrimination protections.
